title: Beyond Prompting: How Real LLM Systems Are Built
subtitle: 23 notebooks show the full stack from training to retrieval
intro: You saved 23 notebooks with 3K stars that go beyond prompting. Most people stop at chat; serious builders train, align, and connect knowledge.
takeaway: Real LLM systems combine cheap fine-tuning, outside knowledge, and careful evaluation — not just bigger prompts.

sections.heading: Analogy: the library intern
sections.body:
Think of a base LLM like a smart intern who read the whole library once.

Fine-tuning is short job training. LoRA means you don't retrain the whole brain, you add a tiny adapter — a few sticky notes that teach a new skill.

RAG is giving the intern a walkie-talkie to the library. Instead of guessing, they look up fresh pages when you ask.

That sets up why builders need both tricks.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: beyond prompting
sections.body:
Prompting alone can't teach private data or keep facts fresh.

The repo shows the full stack: Training with LoRA/QLoRA and 4-bit quantization — quantization means shrinking model weights from 16-bit to 4-bit so LLaMA or Mistral fits on one GPU. Alignment with RLHF — RLHF means learning from human thumbs-up/down on custom datasets. Retrieval with RAG pipelines via LangChain and Knowledge Graphs.

Example: fine-tune Phi on your docs with QLoRA, then add RAG so it cites Neo4j.

But cheap and clever has limits.

sections.heading: What can go wrong?: when shortcuts break
sections.body:
Quantization saves memory but can blur accuracy. A 1-bit model is tiny but forgets nuance.

LoRA adapters can overfit your small dataset and fail on new questions.

RAG can retrieve the wrong page and the LLM will confidently quote it. Without MLflow evaluation — MLflow means tracking scores over time — you won't notice.

So builders test every step: training, alignment, retrieval, and optimization.

steps.narration: Start with base model like LLaMA or Mistral.
Add LoRA adapter with 4-bit quantization to teach cheaply.
Align outputs with RLHF on your human ratings.
Connect RAG to fetch fresh docs at ask time.
Track quality with MLflow before shipping.

options: Adds a small trainable adapter on top
quiz.why: LoRA freezes the base model and trains tiny adapter weights, making fine-tuning cheap.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x and you rely only on 4-bit QLoRA without RAG or evaluation?
options: Hallucinations and stale facts grow unnoticed
quiz.why: Without retrieval and MLflow checks, quantization errors and outdated knowledge compound at scale.

options: Letting the model look up external documents when answering
quiz.why: RAG pipelines fetch relevant docs via LangChain/ChromaDB so answers stay fresh and grounded.
